en.title: Project DNA and product identity
en.summary: What HES is, how its product layers differ, and which principles cannot be bypassed.

sections.heading: Product identity
sections.body: HES Trade Agent is the complete trading-agent product. HES Trade AI is its intelligent brain and conversational assistant, working with the Mother Orchestrator and specialist agents. HES Command Center is the user-facing workspace for communication, observation, commands and control. These names describe different layers and are not interchangeable.
bullets: HOSHYAR is retired as a user-facing product name; legacy technical identifiers remain unchanged until a separately reviewed migration.
The project is designed to be market-, venue-, symbol-, timeframe- and strategy-transferable; each new adapter or profile still needs its own evidence and validation.

sections.heading: Non-negotiable principles
sections.body: Prefer sustainable decision quality over trade frequency. Every capability must have a measurable metric, a reproducible test and traceable evidence. Unknown or missing evidence must not be presented as a verified fact.
bullets: Free-first: no paid or metered hosted LLM API and no remote-model fallback for the Command Center.
Mother evidence readers are authoritative for project facts; the local model may assist with bounded language tasks but is not a trading authority.
Human approval, least privilege, capital protection and fail-closed behavior take precedence over convenience.

sections.heading: Source freshness and authority
sections.body: The local DNA snapshot was synchronized from the canonical Notion page on 2026-11-19T07:16:29Z. Its source verification metadata remains unverified and it is not a live Notion connection; refresh and verify it whenever the canonical source changes.
bullets: Current code, schemas, tests and runtime evidence remain the technical source of truth.
If a source conflicts with live code or an approved checkpoint, record the conflict instead of silently choosing one.

sections.heading: Documentation as a first-class capability
sections.body: Documentation is a versioned, searchable capability inside the existing HES Command Center. It is a curated explanation of project intent and verified technical knowledge, not a second application or a source of trading/runtime truth.
bullets: The library provides Persian, English, German and French; Persian is RTL and the other three locales are LTR.

It covers project DNA and roadmap, architecture, market data and protocol contracts, strategies and indicators, risk and execution boundaries, learning, news and journals, operations, glossary and troubleshooting.
The API is GET-only, locale/schema validated and fail-closed. It cannot read secrets, access accounts, mutate journals or policies, invoke execution or place orders.
Every new capability and architecture decision must update all four locales together, with source provenance, catalog version/changelog and exact-commit tests.

en.title: Roadmap and delivery gates
en.summary: The documented staged path from inventory through local intelligence and approved engineering.

sections.heading: Implementation phases
sections.body: The canonical HES Trade AI roadmap is staged so each phase can be measured before the next is enabled.
bullets: Phase 0 — Inventory and feasibility: inspect the existing VPS, services, Mother/chat, dependencies, security boundaries and dirty checkout. Do not reset or clean the checkout or restart unrelated services.

Phase 1 — Local model benchmark: measure CPU/RAM, latency, context, multilingual quality and concurrent-load impact. If resources or quality are insufficient, report the constraint; do not fall back to paid inference.
Phase 2 — Conversation and memory: extend the existing Mother chat with multilingual multi-turn context, session isolation, controlled durable memory, retrieval provenance and user control.
Phase 3 — Diagnostics and strategy intelligence: provide read-only, evidence-linked explanations over operational and trading records.
Phase 4 — Hypothesis lab: reproducible isolated experiments, baselines, metrics, out-of-sample validation and cost/slippage checks.
Phase 5 — Engineering copilot under approval: minimal patch proposal, tests, review, explicit approval, controlled deployment and rollback.

sections.heading: Release discipline
sections.body: A roadmap item is not complete because code exists. Completion requires the acceptance criteria, tests, provenance and operational boundaries for that item. Staging and production are separate states.
bullets: Do not infer production activation from a staging pass.
Record blockers and unverified dependencies explicitly.
Keep trading execution disabled unless a separate, explicit release gate authorizes it.

sections.heading: Documentation and knowledge-governance gate
sections.body: Documentation is a cross-cutting acceptance gate for every roadmap phase, not a standalone phase that can lag behind implementation.
bullets: Before a capability is called complete, update the DNA/roadmap or relevant reference page and all four dashboard locales in the same reviewed change.
Keep the source register, verification/freshness status, catalog version and change history accurate; explicitly label snapshots that are not live connections.
Run locale completeness, read-only API, responsive desktop/mobile and RTL/LTR browser checks on the exact candidate commit.
A green documentation test does not authorize production deployment or trading; merge, release and rollback remain separate approval gates.

en.title: Architecture and agent responsibilities
en.summary: The existing Mother-centered design and the boundaries between specialists, interface and authority.

sections.heading: Control flow
sections.body: The Mother Orchestrator coordinates specialist evaluation over a shared, validated evidence snapshot. HES Command Center presents status and accepts questions; it is not a second strategy engine or an independent trading authority.
bullets: Data Quality validates source, freshness, gaps and provenance.
Market Structure/Regime describes market context; Signal and Confirmation assess candidate setup evidence.
Risk Gate can veto a candidate and enforce NO_TRADE. Decision and Evaluation record the resulting decision and its evidence.
Execution is a separately gated capability; the current dashboard is read-only and exposes no order-submit route.
Learning Loop evaluates forward decisions, rejected candidates and resolved outcomes without hindsight leakage or metric manipulation.

sections.heading: Authority boundaries
sections.body: The local conversational model is optional and subordinate. It can route bounded intents and explain verified evidence; it cannot replace Mother specialists, change strategy policy, write journals, access exchange accounts or submit orders.
bullets: Reuse existing adapters, readers, APIs, authentication, journal and dashboard; do not create parallel infrastructure without evidence.
A chart or indicator is descriptive unless its specific decision role has been validated and authorized.

en.title: Market data and exchange adapters
en.summary: Separate authoritative analysis data from venue-specific execution connectivity.

sections.heading: Current analysis source
sections.body: The dashboard contract identifies Gate.io Public Spot as the canonical live market-data source. The canonical BTC market is BTC_USDT. Explicitly mapped ETH_USDT and SOL_USDT pairs may be displayed through the shared native adapter, but their strategy/timeframe roles remain descriptive until independently validated.
bullets: Chart and indicator calculations must use the same validated closed-candle batch and its SHA-256 provenance.
Only fresh, fully closed, gap-checked candles are eligible for display or downstream evidence.
This is one public venue source, not a cross-venue consolidated index. News feeds are never a source of candles or indicators.

sections.heading: Analysis versus execution
sections.body: A global chart price is not an executable quote on a trading venue. Data adapters and execution adapters have different contracts and must not be conflated.
bullets: Before any venue adapter can be enabled, validate symbol mapping, venue filters, spread/slippage, risk approval, idempotency and fill reconciliation.
Do not assume that a symbol name or a public market-data connection proves account access or order capability.
Reuse the existing Gate.io reader and native OHLCV path; avoid rebuilding the same data infrastructure.

en.title: Exchange sequence semantics and event ordering
en.summary: Sequence-like fields are opaque until their exact venue and message contract proves otherwise.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: A field named sequence, seq, id, tradeId, u or updateId has no universal meaning. Semantics depend on the exact venue, product, endpoint, channel, message type, field path and protocol version. Numeric shape alone proves neither uniqueness nor ordering, contiguity, gap detection or comparability across reconnects.
bullets: Unknown is a first-class state and is not equivalent to false; unknown never grants a capability.
Trade identity is not ordering. Ordering is not contiguity. Contiguity is not cross-reconnect comparability.
Only documented order-book ranges or links may drive gap detection, and only inside their documented scope.
Exact raw-payload replay can be treated idempotently when the adapter supports it; a repeated opaque number is not automatically a duplicate or conflict.

sections.heading: Tabdeal and cross-venue examples
sections.body: The supplied research report and the project registry classify Tabdeal FAPI/Margin trade.sequence conservatively. The official material reviewed does not define it as a trade ID, stream sequence, gap counter or deduplication key. The official reply recorded by the project owner says not to assume uniqueness, ordering, consecutiveness, replay, gap detection or deduplication; depth sequence is separate and REST reconciliation is approximate.
bullets: Tabdeal broadcast inner trade fields are not fully defined in the reviewed public page; preserve full raw payloads with market, receive time and venue event time.
Binance Spot depth uses documented U/u update ranges and a REST snapshot synchronization procedure; trade IDs are a different contract.
OKX documents prevSeqId/seqId for particular book channels and a maintenance reset; Bybit documents channel-specific u/seq behavior. Coinbase and Kraken have their own channel-specific guarantees.
Do not copy one exchange's sequence rules to another product or channel. Reconnect creates a new session epoch unless the exact contract explicitly allows cross-session comparison.

sections.heading: Required recovery and tests
sections.body: On reconnect, resubscribe and obtain a fresh snapshot when the channel requires it. Keep venue event time separate from local receive time. Schema drift, stale data, checksum failure, corrupt checkpoints or broken documented book linkage must block dependent processing.
bullets: Test exact replay, repeated opaque IDs, documented conflicting identities, missing fields, numeric gaps, backward IDs, timestamp units, reconnect epochs and snapshot resets.
For unknown/non-contiguous fields, random numeric jumps must never produce a missing-event conclusion solely through arithmetic.
Affected stateful strategies remain NO_TRADE_ONLY until a valid resynchronization is proven.

en.title: Strategy, timeframes and indicators
en.summary: How research features support, but do not independently authorize, a trade decision.

sections.heading: Timeframe roles
sections.body: The documented BTC profile assigns 4H and 1H to higher-timeframe context, 15M as setup authority, and 1M as precision refinement. The 1M layer cannot create a setup, change direction or bypass the 15M gate.
bullets: ETH and SOL remain descriptive until their own timeframe-role profiles pass validation.
A timeframe alignment display is evidence, not a prediction or trade authorization.
Strategy panels are read-only projections of canonical evaluators and journals; they must not calculate a competing strategy.

sections.heading: Indicator interpretation
sections.body: Indicators are descriptive features grouped by evidence family to avoid double-counting correlated signals. Regime evidence share is not a predictive probability.
bullets: Trend: EMA relationships/slopes, ADX/DI, Supertrend and Aroon.
Momentum: RSI, MACD, stochastic, Williams %R, ROC and CCI.
Volatility: ATR, Bollinger, Keltner and Donchian measures.
Volume/flow: VWAP, relative volume, OBV, MFI and CMF, only when source volume semantics are valid.
Regime: choppiness and efficiency ratio. Missing volume semantics disables volume-derived indicators only.

en.title: Risk gates and execution boundary
en.summary: Why HOLD and NO_TRADE are valid outcomes and why the dashboard cannot place orders.

sections.heading: Fail-closed decision policy
sections.body: Missing, stale, contradictory or unverified evidence must block the affected decision path. NO_TRADE is an intentional safety outcome, not a system failure or an invitation to lower thresholds.
bullets: Data Quality, Confirmation and Risk Gate cannot be bypassed by the interface, local model, indicators or news.
The Risk Gate may veto a candidate; the system must preserve the reason and evidence reference.
Do not infer a fill, realized outcome or executed trade from a signal or decision record.

sections.heading: Current interface boundary
sections.body: The dashboard contract is read-only: no account access, no order-submit route and no policy or journal mutation. A market-data quote does not prove executable venue pricing.
bullets: Execution remains disabled unless a separately reviewed adapter, risk, approval, idempotency and reconciliation gate is passed.
Never put credentials, tokens, private keys or account identifiers in documentation.
Any future write-capable tool must use least privilege and explicit human approval.

en.title: Training, evaluation and learning loop
en.summary: Reproducible model research and honest measurement without hindsight or metric manipulation.

sections.heading: Model and experiment records
sections.body: A training record should identify the run, data source, time range, sample count, feature schema, label method, chronological split, model artifact hash, parameters, metrics and limitations. A model artifact or successful training run is not proof of a profitable strategy.
bullets: Keep training data and model artifacts separate from source code when appropriate; record immutable hashes and provenance.
Use chronological train/validation/test splits and out-of-sample checks; avoid leakage from future candles or outcomes.
Benchmark resource use and concurrent VPS impact before enabling a local model in production.

sections.heading: Forward evaluation
sections.body: The Learning Loop should evaluate accepted and rejected decisions, missed opportunities, costs and resolved outcomes using canonical forward journals. Preserve the decision as it was made; do not rewrite history.
bullets: Attribute outcomes to the gates and evidence available at decision time.
Do not optimize thresholds retrospectively to fit a historical winner set.
A hypothesis needs preregistered criteria, reproducible isolated tests, baseline comparison and cost/slippage analysis.

en.title: News Radar and decision journal
en.summary: News supplies context; the journal preserves immutable forward evidence.

sections.heading: News intelligence
sections.body: News Radar is contextual evidence, not a signal generator. It must distinguish international, domestic and venue-operational sources and expose coverage, source health and freshness limitations.
bullets: A stale, future-dated, empty or failed source must not be presented as fresh verified coverage.
Gate.io announcements are venue-operational news only; they do not replace the market-data feed.
News cannot originate trade direction, override Confirmation or Risk Gate, or authorize execution.

sections.heading: Decision journal
sections.body: The journal stores forward decisions and their evidence references. It must not infer executed trades or realized outcomes when those facts were not supplied by an authoritative execution record.
bullets: Preserve timestamps, market, timeframe, decision, strategy family, gate/reason, outcome status and evidence hashes as defined by the journal contract.
Distinguish no-trade, rejected candidate, accepted paper decision, executed order and realized outcome.
Use the journal to assess prevented losses and missed opportunities without changing historical decisions.

en.title: Operations, privacy, backup and recovery
en.summary: Operational safety rules for the VPS, documentation updates and future maintenance.

sections.heading: Runtime and deployment
sections.body: The HES core, orchestration, memory and retrieval run on the VPS; browser/mobile clients remain thin. Production changes must be isolated, tested, reviewed and deployed through a controlled release with rollback evidence.
bullets: Do not reset, clean or overwrite a dirty checkout; preserve untracked work and existing release pointers.
Do not restart unrelated services or enable an optional model as a side effect of documentation work.
Staging success and production activation are separate and must be recorded separately.

sections.heading: Privacy and recovery
sections.body: Documentation must never contain secrets or private user data. Backup and recovery instructions must identify scope, encryption, retention, integrity checks and restore verification.
bullets: Use only approved evidence roots and least-privilege readers; never expose credential files through documentation APIs.
Record backup hashes and restore-test evidence; a successful backup command alone does not prove recoverability.
After a reconnect or corrupted state, rebuild from validated snapshots rather than guessing missing sequence or checkpoint values.

en.title: Glossary
en.summary: Consistent terminology used across HES documentation and the dashboard.

sections.heading: Market-data and protocol terms
sections.body: Use these meanings consistently in code, reports and translations.
bullets: Event identity: a documented key that identifies an event within a declared scope.
Ordering: a documented relationship that establishes which event precedes another.
Contiguity: a documented rule that allows missing events to be inferred from a broken range or link.
Scope: the venue/product/endpoint/channel/message/field/protocol tuple to which a guarantee applies.
Sequence epoch: a session or synchronization period; values from different epochs are not comparable unless documented.
Provenance: source, retrieval context, timestamps, schema and cryptographic hashes that explain where evidence came from.

sections.heading: Decision and safety terms
sections.body: Safety labels must not be softened by translation.
bullets: NO_TRADE: no trade is authorized for the evaluated evidence and policy state.
HOLD: a release or decision gate remains unresolved.
Fail closed: block the affected operation when required evidence or validation is missing.
Read-only: data may be inspected and explained, but not changed or acted upon.
Descriptive-only: a feature provides context but has no independent signal or policy authority.

en.title: Troubleshooting and FAQ
en.summary: A safe diagnostic path for common dashboard, data, chat and protocol states.

sections.heading: Dashboard and market-data checks
sections.body: Start with the reported status and the exact evidence reference. Check source identity, freshness, closed-candle state, gap count and batch hash before interpreting a chart or indicator.
bullets: If the chart is blocked or stale, inspect the health endpoint, dashboard logs and canonical Gate.io reader; do not substitute cached or manually fabricated candles.
If an indicator is unavailable, verify that its input batch matches the chart batch. Missing volume semantics should disable volume-derived features only.
If a mapped symbol is descriptive-only, do not treat its chart as a validated strategy profile.

sections.heading: Command Center and protocol questions
sections.body: The Command Center is read-only and uses the existing local authentication/session boundary. Documentation cannot unlock the chat, change policy or enable execution.
bullets: If chat access is unavailable, verify the locally configured access token and session state; never paste credentials into a report or documentation page.
If a sequence value repeats or jumps, consult the exact venue/product/channel registry record. Do not infer a lost trade from arithmetic.
After a required stream reconnect, resubscribe and rebuild state from the documented snapshot procedure. Keep dependent stateful processing blocked until synchronization is verified.
HOLD and NO_TRADE are valid outcomes when evidence is missing, stale or contradictory; do not lower thresholds to make a panel appear healthy.

sections.heading: Escalation evidence
sections.body: When a fault persists, collect only the minimum non-secret evidence needed to reproduce it.
bullets: Record timestamp and timezone, component/version, venue/product/channel, symbol/timeframe, status/reason code and relevant content hash.
Redact tokens, account identifiers, private keys, personal data and full private payloads before sharing.
Preserve the original event and log; do not rewrite journals, checkpoints or historical decisions to hide the failure.
